findings.claim: The 'Route kind' decision says a GET with Upgrade: websocket 'resolves only against WebSocket routes'. That contradicts frozen D-441, which says an Upgrade: websocket request to a path with no WebSocket registration is resolved as an ordinary GET: it reaches the GET route, or else gets method mismatch or no match. If a worker follows the decision as written, such a request returns no match (404) even when a GET route exists, and the D-441 router test fails. The section also claims it 'contradict[s] no frozen item'.
findings.suggested_fix: Reword: a GET with Upgrade: websocket resolves first against WebSocket routes and, when no WebSocket pattern matches the path, falls back to HTTP routes as a plain GET without upgrading (D-441). A plain request resolves only against HTTP routes.

findings.claim: The precedence decision limits WebSocket-only to 'a GET without Upgrade'. Frozen D-069 and object.md section 3.3 apply it to any request without Upgrade to a WS-only path, so with this decision POST, HEAD and the rest get 405 instead. This is an unstated narrowing of a frozen item. HEAD then differs from GET (405 vs 426), which goes against RFC 9110 section 9.3.2 (HEAD is identical to GET without the content). The decision also leaves open whether a WebSocket route adds GET, automatic HEAD or OPTIONS to the 405 Allow set and the automatic-OPTIONS Allow set. If it does, Allow lists GET/HEAD for a resource that just answered 405/426 to them. If it does not, OPTIONS to a WS-only path returns an Allow without GET.
findings.suggested_fix: State explicitly which methods get WebSocket-only on a WS-only path: GET and HEAD without Upgrade, or every method as D-069 literally says. If the choice narrows D-069, record it as a narrowing, not as 'no contradiction'. Define whether WebSocket routes contribute to the Allow sets of D-061 and D-064 (e.g. a WS route contributes GET only, and HEAD only if HEAD also yields 426). Add router tests for HEAD, POST and OPTIONS to a WS-only path.

findings.claim: The 'Markers' decision has wave 2 remove the 'automatic HEAD method value' marker (the req.method() value during automatic HEAD, routing.md:119). Frozen D-398 assigns that decision and that marker to wave 3. The two waves would both own the same (미확정) item, and wave 2 would have to decide a Request behaviour before Request exists (wave 3). As r1 W2-004 noted, the //, trailing-slash, case and TRACE/CONNECT markers at routing.md:71,91 are config-API-name markers, so no marker about routing behaviour actually remains for wave 2 to remove.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop 'automatic HEAD method value' from the wave 2 marker list and leave it to D-398. Say that wave 2 documents the decided //, trailing-slash, case and TRACE/CONNECT semantics in routing.md and keeps the '설정 API (미확정)' name markers for wave 3.

findings.claim: The precedence decision puts the D-052 rejection (400) as the first step 'the router evaluates'. D-390 says a lookup returns exactly one of six variants, and none of them is an invalid path or 400. The path-validation decision says adapters call the validator before routing. So it is unclear whether the router lookup itself validates and how it reports a rejection without a seventh variant.
findings.suggested_fix: Say that path validation runs before the router lookup and reports its rejection outside the match result (e.g. the validator's own result or exception). The lookup assumes a validated, once-decoded path and returns only the six D-390 variants.

findings.claim: D-067 and D-070 require wave 2 to decide the semantics of the TRACE/CONNECT enable policy and of the //, trailing-slash and case options. The Wave decisions section depends on 'while their routing is not enabled' but decides none of these. For example, it does not say whether registering a TRACE route while the policy is off is a configuration error or a dormant route, whether the option collapses // or treats it as an empty segment, or whether trailing-slash-insensitive matching also changes the D-056/D-057 conflict checks. Two workers could produce different router behaviour.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a decision per policy: what enabling TRACE/CONNECT allows (explicit routes only, Method.any() unchanged), and what a registration made while it is disabled does. Define the effect of each normalisation option on matching and on conflict detection at freeze.

findings.claim: The note for wave 3 has the in-memory adapter mirror TinyHttpd's absolute-form rewrite, but says nothing about authority-form CONNECT (CONNECT host:443). TinyHttpd answers it with a transport-level 501 (D-422). Under D-442 the in-memory adapter would answer 400, so the 'identically on both adapters' clause of D-442 still fails for this target.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend the note: the in-memory adapter answers authority-form CONNECT with 501 as TinyHttpd does, or the case is excluded from D-442's identical-result clause and recorded under D-020.
